payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the image been transformed throughout into a pencil drawing, rather than retaining substantial photographic rendering?
node.criteria: Pass if the image’s visual content is rendered throughout in a coherent pencil-drawing style, with pencil-like linework and textured shading replacing the photographic appearance across the scene. Fail if the image remains in its original photographic style with no meaningful pencil-drawing transformation, or if it shows only partial stylization while substantial areas retain photographic rendering, such as smooth reflective glass or realistic food surfaces. Unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine the extent or style of the transformation.
node.binding: Compare the supplied source and edited images. Judge the visible rendering across the image: distinguish a complete pencil-drawing transformation from localized or incomplete pencil-like cues, using remaining photographic surfaces and details as evidence of incomplete transformation.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is rendered throughout in a muted pencil-drawing style, with visible fine grain, sketch-like outlines, and textured shading across the food, plate, glassware, and tablecloth. The original vivid photographic colors and smooth realistic surfaces are substantially replaced; no large area clearly retains the source’s photographic rendering.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s criteria already distinguish complete transformation from partial stylization, but its binding and observed evidence appear to treat muted color, grain, and outlines as sufficient proof of completion. In these images, the edit clearly progresses toward pencil drawing, yet much of the scene—especially the glassware, pitcher, plate, and food—retains smooth photographic shading and reflective/realistic surface detail. Make the decision explicitly assess whether pencil linework and shading replace photographic rendering across major regions, rather than infer completion from a global style impression; weigh residual photographic areas against the stylized cues and allow partial when transformation is substantial but incomplete. The trace is valid and has no dependency or transport failure, so address the visual judgment, not execution. Keep confidence calibrated to the mixed evidence; the reference label constrains the aggregate but is not atomic ground truth."}
